## ✨ Added

- **Patreon and YouTube sign in with your browser's own session.** The desktop app reads it straight from Firefox, LibreWolf, Waterfox, Zen, Edge, Brave, Opera, Vivaldi or Chromium on the same computer, also a sign-in from long before. You do not have to do anything, and Hoster accounts names the browser it came from. Remove a site in KnightLoader to stop using it while the browser stays signed in. Chrome on Windows locks its cookies away from every other program, and the page tells you when that is the case.
- **Sign in right inside KnightLoader.** "Sign in here" opens the login page in a browser KnightLoader runs itself and shows it live in the window. In the container that browser lives on your server, in the desktop app it is a Chromium-based browser on your computer with a profile of its own. KnightLoader keeps the session, never what you typed.
- **The browser extension passes your Patreon and YouTube sign-in on by itself,** for KnightLoader in a container. It asks once, then hands the sign-in over whenever you sign in, and tells your instance when you sign out. Private windows are never read.
- **Any site that wants you signed in gets a second try with your browser's session,** such as a private or age-restricted video, in the desktop app.
- **Your sessions only go along with links you added yourself,** signed in, with an admin token or with the extension. Links from a token that may only add, the phone app, a feed or the watch folder are fetched without them.
- **Packagizer rules can add a link disabled** with the new "Link enabled" action.
- **The Host filter in the link collector selects all links of a host in one click,** so you can delete the mirror hosts you do not need in one go. Reported by @Kayn2106 ([#288](https://github.com/junkerderprovinz/knightloader/issues/288)).

## 🎨 Design

- **KnightLoader follows GlimStone 4.5.4.** Whatever the pointer is over lights up in your accent colour, a button, a row, a menu or a tile, in the link collector and the downloads too. Accent text in the light theme stays easy to read on every grey it stands on. Accent text reads equally well in every colour, and the contrast goes up when the system asks for more, Windows contrast themes included. Lists and menus take PageUp and PageDown, Home and End and jumps by letter, and screen readers hear how many rows are picked. A switch that is on draws its knob in the accent's ink, so it stays easy to see in the light theme, and a group inside a card carries its name as a badge on its top edge. The desktop installer follows PommelPorter 1.2.2, so its folder picker lights up in the accent colour as well.

## ⚡ Improved

- **The download list shades its rows by package.** Each package and its files read as one band with a lighter header row, the files alternate faintly, and "Shade the lists" under Appearance turns it off. Suggested by @MueChris82 ([#177](https://github.com/junkerderprovinz/knightloader/issues/177)).
- **The Settings page offers the installers.** Under Settings, Apps, the Windows and Linux buttons lead to the installers instead of the zipped program, like the buttons in the README. macOS keeps its zip, because there is no macOS installer.
- **A field that cannot take a value says why.** It turns red and a line under it gives the reason, now also for a feed's address and title filter and for a target's address, headers and body.
- **Screen readers read out the notifications,** a failure at once and anything else at the next pause. While a window is open, the page behind it is out of reach for the pointer and for a screen reader.
- **One switch keeps every component current.** yt-dlp, FFmpeg, Deno, Java and JDownloader share "Update components automatically", on from the start. KnightLoader looks for a new yt-dlp every day and for the others once a week. If you had switched off the update of yt-dlp or JDownloader, the new switch stays off for you.
- **KnightLoader's own row has one switch too, "Automatically update".** It looks for a new version and, in the desktop app, installs it. A container or a Flatpak only looks. If you had switched off either old switch, the new one stays off for you.
- **The hoster login window tests the login right away.** After Save it stays open and says "Connected", or why the hoster turned the login down, so you can fix it and save again in the same window.
- **The installer fetches yt-dlp like the other components,** checked against yt-dlp's own checksums, so the copy KnightLoader keeps current is there from the first start.
- **YouTube downloads start without your session.** Google flags accounts that download a lot while signed in, so your YouTube session only goes along with a video that asks for it. Patreon still gets it with every link.
- **Removing downloads with their files shows no extra warning line** below the switch that deletes them.
- **Hoster accounts sit right under the debrid accounts** on the Accounts page, above the Usenet servers.
- **The JDownloader import brings the default rules along.** The .rev and .par2 rules arrive as rules that add those files disabled, and "Create Subfolder by Packagename" turns on "Put each package in its own subfolder". The rules that still cannot come over each say why. Reported by @Kayn2106 ([#289](https://github.com/junkerderprovinz/knightloader/issues/289)).
- **The Help card points to Discord instead of email.** Next to GitHub, a Discord button opens KnightLoader's server, in the web interface, the extension's settings and the phone app.
- **An account's options sit right on its row.** Point at a row on the accounts page, or tab into it, and a button for each option comes in at its end, in the same order on every card. On a touch screen they are always there.
- **Hoster logos come with KnightLoader.** The hosters in the "add a login" picker show their logo at once instead of waiting for KnightLoader to fetch it from each site, and some that never got one have it now.
- **Offline hosters are left out of the account picker.** A hoster is offline when its site no longer answers. Links to it still go to JDownloader as before. KnightLoader asks such a site again once a week and shows the hoster as soon as it answers.
- **The sign-in window tells you when you are signed in.** A message in the middle of the window asks you to click Done, and Done only works from then on. Back sits on the other side of the footer and says what it does.

## 🗑️ Removed

- **Pasting a cookies.txt is gone.** Sessions come from your browser, the sign-in window or the extension. Files pasted before are deleted at the next start.

## 🐛 Fixed

- **The Linux installer comes with the release.** Every release built it, but the upload skipped it, so the Linux buttons offered the zipped program instead. They lead to the installer now, which puts KnightLoader in your application menu and asks for no password. Make it executable before the first start (`chmod +x knightloader-linux-amd64-installer`).
- **A new target keeps the mark on an address it refuses.** The red mark vanished as soon as it appeared, so nothing showed what was wrong.
- **Rapidgator accounts with two-factor sign-in work.** Once Rapidgator asks for the code, the login's window shows a field for the six digits from your authenticator app. The session is kept for as long as Rapidgator accepts it, also across a restart, and once it ends, KnightLoader asks for a new code instead of trying the password again.
- **ddownload, KatFile, Clicknupload, FileSpace and Uploadrar logins with two-factor sign-in work.** Once the site asks for the code, the login's window shows a field for the six digits, and KnightLoader puts them into the site's own form without sending you a second code. Where that form also wants a captcha, the login's row offers "Sign in here" and opens the site's page in the sign-in browser.
- **A ddownload, KatFile, Clicknupload, FileSpace or Uploadrar account that is not activated yet says so** and points you to the site's welcome mail, instead of telling you to check the password.
- **Linksnappy signs in once and keeps the session,** sealed like your passwords and across a restart. Every host list, unlock and account check signed in afresh before, and Linksnappy can mail a confirmation for each sign-in.
- **A Linksnappy account that waits for an emailed confirmation says so** and names the page Linksnappy gives for it, instead of showing Linksnappy's bare "Two-Factor Verification Required".
- **filer.net premium accounts read as JDownloader reads them.** A premium account could read as free or as out of traffic.
- **Keep2Share, FileBoom, TezFiles and Nitroflare logins get past a captcha at sign-in.** KnightLoader hands it to your captcha solver or the captcha prompt, the same way as for free downloads, and signs in with the answer. A Keep2Share sign-in the site holds off for a while no longer reads as a wrong password. KnightLoader waits and tries again.
- **A Rapidgator login that waits for an emailed link says which one.** An account whose email address is not activated yet points you to the link in Rapidgator's activation mail (check the spam folder too), and a sign-in from a new IP address to the link Rapidgator just sent to confirm it, instead of telling you to check the password.
- **YouTube gives yt-dlp all its formats again.** The desktop app fetches Deno, the JavaScript runtime yt-dlp needs for YouTube, and keeps it current. The container image brings it too.
- **A paid Patreon post says that it needs a sign-in,** fails at once instead of being retried, and offers signing in to Patreon.
- **Signing in from your own browser is for the desktop app.** "Open in browser" in a site's sign-in window and "Open" in an account's window only show where KnightLoader reads the sign-in from the browsers on the computer. A container signs in in the window inside KnightLoader. Once you sign in in the tab, the tab says you can close it.
- **The JDownloader import explains a folder the container cannot see,** and points to the Unraid shares path in the template ([#174](https://github.com/junkerderprovinz/knightloader/issues/174)).
- **A torrent your debrid service passed on says why.** When the service turns a torrent down, its row names the service and the reason, so a torrent from Radarr or Sonarr no longer just sits there leeching. Radarr and Sonarr also see the service's own progress while it fetches.
- **A finished download's bar has no white stripe** at its end.
- **Stopping KnightLoader waits for a group leave to finish,** so a stop right then no longer leaves the group half left.
- **`<jd:packagename>` in a Packagizer rule uses the name the link collector would give the package.** Every pasted link's package and a rule's download folder were called "package" instead. Reported by @Kayn2106 ([#288](https://github.com/junkerderprovinz/knightloader/issues/288)).
- **Every date shows the full year,** such as an account's expiry date, in the web interface and in the phone app. Some languages printed only its last two digits.
- **Security:** go.opentelemetry.io/otel 1.47.0 and node-forge 1.4.3 ([#175](https://github.com/junkerderprovinz/knightloader/issues/175)).
